problem:
Consider the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}]x(t).$ Which of the following vectors are solutions to this equation?

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}(t)=[\begin{aligned}t \\ t+1\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Here, we need to substitute each vector into the given matrix differential equation and check if it results in a true statement.

For ${x}_{1}(t)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{({e}^{-t})}^{′} \\ {(0)}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-{e}^{-t} \\ 0\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for ${x}_{2}(t)$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{(0)}^{′} \\ {({e}^{2t})}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2{e}^{2t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{2t}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for ${x}_{3}(t)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{(t)}^{′} \\ {(t+1)}^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t \\ t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t \\ t+1\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}-t \\ 2(t+1)\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ only".
